manifest.title: Prometheus, Grafana, and Alertmanager
manifest.tagline: TiDB's own metrics detect a slow query storm, a write hot spot, a store outage, and a connection surge
manifest.pattern: platform and SRE teams that will not approve a new database until its metrics, alerts, and traces land in the observability stack they already run

metrics.label: Queries per second
metrics.howMeasured: Prometheus instant query sum(rate(tidb_executor_statement_total[60s])) against the demo-local Prometheus, polled once per tick

metrics.label: Query p99 latency
metrics.howMeasured: Prometheus instant query histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(tidb_server_handle_query_duration_seconds_bucket[60s])) by (le)) * 1000, polled once per tick

metrics.label: TiKV write rate
metrics.howMeasured: Prometheus instant query sum(rate(tikv_raftstore_write_cmd_total{type="put"}[60s])) by (instance), polled once per tick, max across instances

metrics.label: Active connections
metrics.howMeasured: Prometheus instant query sum(tidb_server_connections), polled once per tick

metrics.label: Time to detect (last fault)
metrics.howMeasured: webhook receipt timestamp minus fault injection timestamp, recorded in-process by the runner

metrics.label: Time to recover (last fault)
metrics.howMeasured: Alertmanager resolved timestamp from GET /api/v2/alerts minus the clear-faults control timestamp, recorded by the runner

phases.label: Steady state
phases.narration: This is a TiDB cluster under a normal read/write mix, already scraped by the Prometheus and Grafana you saw start with the playground.

phases.label: Slow query storm
phases.narration: Now a bad deploy ships a query that forces a full table scan. Watch p99 latency climb on the same Grafana panel your team already watches.

phases.label: Write hot spot
phases.narration: Here's a classic hot-spot write pattern: monotonically increasing keys landing on one TiKV Region.

phases.label: TiKV store outage
phases.narration: This is the failure every platform team asks about: what happens when a node just goes down.

phases.label: Connection surge
phases.narration: And a connection leak in a client library, which is one of the most common pages we get.

phases.label: Recovery
phases.narration: Every alert we just saw resolves on its own once the fault clears, with no manual dashboard edits.

phases.label: Wrap-up
phases.narration: Four faults, four alerts, four resolutions, all through the Prometheus and Alertmanager you already run.

checks.label: Slow query storm alert fired
checks.description: The local slow-query PromQL rule fires and the webhook receiver logs arrival within the rule's for window plus one scrape interval

checks.label: Write hot spot alert fired
checks.description: The local TiKV CPU PromQL rule fires within its for window plus one scrape interval

checks.label: Store outage alert fired
checks.description: The local store-down PromQL rule fires within its for window plus one scrape interval

checks.label: Connection surge alert fired
checks.description: The local connection-count PromQL rule fires within its for window plus one scrape interval

checks.label: All alerts resolved after clearing
checks.description: Alertmanager reports every alert in status resolved within two evaluation intervals of clear-faults

controls.label: Inject slow query storm
controls.description: Starts runSlowQueryStorm and moves to phase slow-query-storm

controls.label: Inject write hot spot
controls.description: Starts runWriteHotSpot and moves to phase write-hot-spot

controls.label: Inject TiKV store outage
controls.description: Starts stopTikvStore and moves to phase store-outage

controls.label: Inject connection surge
controls.description: Starts runConnectionSurge and moves to phase connection-surge

controls.label: Clear all faults
controls.description: Calls clearAllFaults, restarts any stopped TiKV store, moves to phase recovery

environment.notes: local: tiup playground v8.5.8 (pd/tikv/tidb/ticdc/tiflash) + demo-local Prometheus/Alertmanager in Docker federating from the playground's own Prometheus. Recording session only: alert-rules.yml for: shortened from 30s to 10s to keep the featured trace in the 3-6 minute target range (committed file stays at 30s)
